lesson.title: Generate, then check
lesson.subtitle: Facts, level, bias and local fit, before it reaches pupils

video.title: Generate, then check
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds, one recurring teacher character. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Ms Amina Bello — primary teacher, Nigeria (main character)
Ms Salma Haddad — secondary maths teacher (cameo)
Narrator — the Darsi voice (warm, peer to peer)

chapters.label: What checking catches, and the lab

scenes.visual: Amina at the staff-room table, delighted: a quiz scrolls up her phone in seconds. Her smile fades as three lines get a red underline: rice as body-building food, pizza and blueberries, and long, hard words.
scenes.animation: The quiz scrolls fast; the three underlines draw one by one as they are said.
scenes.narration: Twenty quiz questions on healthy eating, in ten seconds! Then I read them. One says rice is a body-building food. The examples are pizza and blueberries. And the words are far too hard for Primary Four.

scenes.visual: Paper-grey card. The Darsi mark pops in, then the course name, the lesson title and a yellow ‘AI’ track chip.
scenes.animation: Mark scales 0→100% with a small overshoot (≤ 200 ms); title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: generate, then check, before anything reaches your pupils.

scenes.visual: A draft machine prints question cards, example cards and explanation cards at speed. Each card lands with a ‘Draft’ stamp on it.
scenes.animation: Cards fly out (1.5 s); the ‘Draft’ stamp thumps onto each (150 ms).
scenes.narration: AI is a fast first-draft machine: questions, examples, explanations, in seconds. But it predicts what sounds likely, and it can’t see your class. So everything it makes is a draft until you’ve checked it.

scenes.visual: A checklist on a clipboard with four numbered checks: facts (a textbook), level (a ruler), bias (a balance), local fit (a market basket).
scenes.animation: Each check ticks in as it is said (300 ms).
scenes.narration: Check four things. Facts: is it true? Check the textbook. Level: are the words and difficulty right for this age? Bias: who’s in it, who’s left out, is every doctor a man? Local fit: our foods, names, money and seasons.

scenes.visual: Amina pastes a textbook page into a chat and types the instruction under it. The answer that comes back has small arrows pointing to lines on that page.
scenes.animation: The page slides into the chat; the instruction types out; arrows draw from the answer to the page.
scenes.narration: You can also ground it in your own source. Paste in a textbook page and say: “Answer only from this page. If it isn’t there, say so.” Now answers should come from a page you trust and can check.

scenes.visual: Clean white card with the AI track chip. A flow: a question, a search through a stack of documents, an answer, and the source document highlighted.
scenes.animation: Nodes appear left to right, 300 ms apart, with arrows drawing between them.
scenes.narration: That’s called grounding: tying an answer to a source you give it. Some tools search your documents first, then answer from what they found and show where. That’s called RAG: retrieval-augmented generation.

scenes.visual: The school newsletter: a volunteer types it quickly; the head teacher reads it line by line with a pen, then signs it before it goes home in pupils’ bags.
scenes.animation: Pages fly out of the typewriter; the pen moves down the page; the signature draws itself.
scenes.narration: Think of the school newsletter. A volunteer can draft it fast. But before it goes home to parents, the head teacher reads every line, because her name is on it. AI drafts; you’re the editor.

scenes.visual: Ms Salma pops in holding a textbook page and her phone, eyebrow raised. Three answer cards drop in below her.
scenes.animation: Character slides in from the side; answer cards drop in with a small bounce.
scenes.narration: Quick check! I told the AI: “Answer only from this textbook page.” Is its answer now guaranteed correct?

scenes.visual: The card ‘No, still check it against the page’ gets a check badge. Two columns: what grounding does (fewer mistakes, easier to check) and what it can’t do (stop misreading, fix a wrong page).
scenes.animation: Check badge pops (150 ms); the columns fill as they are said.
scenes.narration: No: still check it against the page. Grounding makes mistakes rarer and easier to spot. But it can still misread the page, mix in other things it learned, or quote the wrong part. And if the page is wrong or out of date, so is the answer.

scenes.visual: Three AI-made worksheet snippets, each with a red pen fix: a story with only male doctors gets a woman doctor; dollars and apples become naira and mangoes; ‘precipitation’ becomes ‘rain’.
scenes.animation: The red pen strikes and rewrites each one; a small clock shows one minute per fix.
scenes.narration: A story where every doctor is a man and every cook a woman: fix it. Prices in dollars and apples, not naira and mangoes: change them. A Primary Two text with words like “precipitation”: simplify it. Each fix takes a minute.

scenes.visual: A phone screen with the lab: a question box with suggested questions, the school’s documents ranked by score, an answer quoted from the best document with its source, and an answer made without sources for comparison.
scenes.animation: Score bars fill; the best document lights up; the quote appears with its source line.
scenes.narration: In the app, ask about a school: exams, the bus, lunch. The AI searches the school’s documents, then quotes the one it used, or says it can’t find it instead of guessing. Compare the answer without sources, then edit a document and ask again.

scenes.visual: Amina holds up a worksheet with one error circled in red. Three answer cards appear beside her.
scenes.animation: Cards bounce in one by one.
scenes.narration: Your turn. An AI drafted my worksheet, and a mistake reached my pupils. Whose responsibility is it?

scenes.visual: The first card gets the check badge, then the screen resolves into four summary lines and an orange takeaway bar.
scenes.animation: Lines tick in 250 ms apart; the takeaway bar slides up.
scenes.narration: Amina’s: a person stays responsible for everything that reaches pupils. Remember: AI drafts; you check facts, level, bias and local fit. Grounding helps, but you still check. Generate fast, then check carefully.

scenes.visual: Amina’s classroom: pairs bend over a worksheet and their textbook, circling errors in pencil. On the board: ‘Evidence, not speed’.
scenes.animation: Circles draw around errors; a pair holds up their sheet with page numbers written beside each circle.
scenes.narration: Try it in class tomorrow: play “Find the mistakes”. Give pairs an AI-made worksheet with a few planted mistakes. They check it against the textbook and circle every error. The best evidence wins, not the fastest pair.

checkpoints.prompt: “Answer only from this textbook page.” Is the answer now guaranteed correct?

options.text: No, still check it against the page
Yes: it can only use the page

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — grounding makes mistakes rarer and easier to spot, but the AI can still misread the page or add things.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — the AI can still misread the page, mix in other things, or quote the wrong part. Check it against the page.

checkpoints.prompt: An AI drafted Amina’s worksheet, and a mistake reached her pupils. Whose responsibility is it?
checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — an AI tool can’t be responsible. The teacher who uses it checks it and answers for what reaches pupils.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — an AI tool can’t answer to parents or pupils. The teacher who uses it stays responsible, so she checks first.
